content:
The face adjacency graph of the octahedron is the cube graph \(Q_3\), which is bipartite with two parts of size \(4\).

The even labels \(2,4,6,8\) cannot be adjacent to each other, so they must occupy one entire bipartition class. Thus:

- Choose which bipartition class gets the evens: \(2\) ways.
- Assign the evens: \(4!\) ways.
- The odds \(1,3,5,7\) go to the other class.

The only forbidden adjacency is \(6\) adjacent to \(3\). Given the position of \(6\), exactly \(3\) of the \(4\) odd vertices are adjacent to it, so \(3\) must go to the unique nonadjacent odd vertex. The remaining three odds can be assigned in \(3!\) ways.

Thus the number of valid labeled cube graphs is
\[
2\cdot 4!\cdot 3! = 2\cdot 24\cdot 6 = 288.
\]

Since all labels are distinct, no nontrivial rotation fixes a labeling. The octahedron has \(24\) rotational symmetries, so the number of inequivalent labelings is
\[
\frac{288}{24}=12.
\]

\[
\boxed{12}
\]
